name: Règles d'urbanisme (PLU)
author: ArchiSimple
description: Reads the planning rules that apply to a French plot: the regime, the document in force and its zone, prescriptions, easements and risks, with a link to the regulation — opened at the zone's page where the deployment runs the companion service, whose reading of the written regulation (on request) gives written rules to confirm, edit or set aside; under the national rules (RNU) and a carte communale, the coded rules, the Site boundary's edges, the R.111-15, R.111-16 and R.111-17 checks, the neighbours' height for R.111-28 and the setback bands; the theoretical buildable area — the Site boundary less the confirmed setbacks and the plan's exclusion areas (espace boisé classé and emplacement réservé; the others, limited constructibility among them, on your say), in pieces and with holes, with each cut, its source and the area it takes, and a height held to a band — drawn on the plan, the areas taken out in translucent red that you can hide, its envelope as a volume in 3D, with the rules it applies and those it does not; the written heights a règlement holds to a strip along the limits (« 2 m high within 5 m of the boundary »), which lift the setback they stand in once confirmed, and the candidate rules decided automatically — another sector, other communes, a reference, « not regulated » — folded under their own heading with one click to bring one back; the regulation sheet's content for Print & PDF; drawn prescriptions with a number and hand-entered rules to confirm, edit or set aside, saved in the project; the emprise au sol and surface de plancher under their French definitions, the footprint budget, extension caps, a capacity estimate and indicative procedure flags; the programme warning that replaces Urban Rules; the assistant's questions on the plot (a storey more, the street distance, the maximum height, what is left to build), each limit cited from the report; the planning figures of every parked design variation; the document in force watched by the companion service, which tells an open project within the hour that the GPU has published a new version and offers « unchanged in the new version — confirm again » for a written rule whose passage and limit did not change; and the reading kept in the project, so a project opened elsewhere or offline shows its planning rules at once, dated, and says what changed when it is read again. The panel draws the plot top view with the edges lettered and the measured distances, the edge list and the envelope's height section; the Surfaces view is a headline figure, the emprise definition as a choice of three cards, the budget as a bar and folded rows.
